It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing a world where political powers grow cold toward the Gospel and seek to claim authority that belongs to the King alone, and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the boundaries between civil authority and the headship of Christ in this hour? [13, 178, 252, 1331, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by the sight of “savage wolves” who use human law as a “scourge” against the faithful, or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul in the truth that “history is His story”—a single, cohesive account of God’s glory where “not one human sinner or demonic power will ever succeed in his rebellion” against the King? [1, 13, 20, 92, 163, 262, 1143, 1283, 1301, 1405, 1425, 1471, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many seek “diplomatic relations” with the culture to avoid the “scars” of the cross, we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Lord personally governs the “vicissitudes of life” by reminding us that our “citizenship is in heaven” [11, 15, 19, 21, 26, 27, 28, 38, 41, 132, 1197, 1313, 1316, 1320, 1326, 1426, 1503, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the tension between church and state is not an “administrative anomaly” but is subject to the “decree from God” who “raises up kings, then pulls them from their thrones when they have served His administration” [15, 68, 158, 162, 237, 249, 384, 694, 1143, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The Sovereignty of God Over All Thrones**

**Verse**
“The LORD has established His throne in heaven, And His kingdom rules over all” (Psalm 103:19). [31, 42, 68, 163, Conversation History]. “ ‘God has numbered your kingdom and put an end to it.… You have been weighed on the scales and found deficient’ ” (Daniel 5:26–27). [28, 914, 1061, 1143, 1402, 1720, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Scriptures reveal that God is the “universal King” who “mediates His rulership through His Son,” and no earthly leader is an absolute law unto himself [31, 178, 181, Conversation History]. While Pharaoh “insolently and arrogantly rejected” the Lord, God used the ten plagues to show that “whatever royal authority Pharaoh had, it had been because of God’s sovereign and providential control,” as the Lord “dismantled” the world power of the day to deliver His people for worship [170, 288, 1142, 1221, 1229, Conversation History]. Similarly, Daniel remained a faithful slave to God even in a “pagan Babylonian society,” for he recognized that “Christ ultimately crushes the kingdoms of men and establishes His own” [9, 23, 1370, Conversation History]. Reformed theology—echoed by **John MacArthur**—asserts that “nothing thwarts any aspect of His plan,” for the Master “harnesses the deeds of the wicked to accomplish His good and perfect ends” [5, 11, 21, 64, 1132, 1143, 1352, 1353, 1515, 1567, 1616, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “trade in your worry for trust,” knowing that “the Word of our God stands forever” even when “earthly kingdoms go the way of all flesh” (Isaiah 40:8; Daniel 5:26) [11, 16, 21, 28, 29, 39, 94, 121, 201, 1306, 1408, 1460, 1515, 1684, Conversation History]. Recognize that “he who trusts in his own heart is a fool,” and you must instead “tremble at My word,” for “there is no authority except from God” (Proverbs 28:26; Isaiah 66:2; Romans 13:1) [11, 15, 75, 79, 131, 251, 851, 1039, 1143, 1184, 1313, 1342, 1381, 1406, 1422, 1473, 1503, 1515, 1532, 1709, 1720, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Theocracy vs. Pilgrimage**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, Israel was a “theocratic nation” where “national greatness” was a “temporal sign” of God’s favor, and kings were commanded to “write for himself a copy of this law” to keep his heart from being “lifted up above his brethren” (Deuteronomy 17:18, 20) [6, 409, 420, 421, 1313, 1353, 1519, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “victory,” revealing that we are “sojourners and pilgrims” whose “citizenship is in heaven,” and our ultimate allegiance is to the King who said, “ ‘My kingdom is not of this world’ ” (John 18:36; Philippians 3:20; 1 Peter 2:11) [13, 20, 21, 26, 27, 28, 32, 38, 142, 440, 1023, 1028, 1113, 1116, 1203, 1313, 1320, 1402, 1426, 1431, 1491, 1515, 1529, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: The Mandate of Apostolic Defiance**

**Verse**
“But Peter and the other apostles answered and said: ‘We ought to obey God rather than men’ ” (Acts 5:29). [48, 682, 808, 875, 914, 1021, 1074, 1130, 1176, 1205, 1247, 1249, 1256, 1300, 1431, 1529, 1720, Conversation History]. “But the midwives feared God, and did not do as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the male children alive” (Exodus 1:17). [1211, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **Paul Washer**—teaches that “salvation is a supernatural work of God,” and the church has a “binding and authoritative mandate” to herald the truth regardless of civil prohibition [11, 24, 251, 260, 280, 429, 557, 561, 803, 822, 1091, 1503, Conversation History]. When the Sanhedrin—the “highest religious court in Israel”—was “riddled with injustice” and sought to “silence” the message of the cross, the apostles established that the church must “refuse to yield submission” to any authority that forbids what God commands [11, 15, 19, 68, 130, 1092, 1130, 1144, 1316, 1422, 1431, 1528, 1636, 1638, 1720, Conversation History]. This is prefigured in the Hebrew midwives who “feared God” more than Pharaoh’s murderous decree, proving that “the Lord’s personal and direct involvement in the affairs of men” preserves His people through their obedience [1211, 1218, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “be bold in our God to speak to you the gospel of God in much conflict,” knowing that “cowardice and authentic faith are antithetical” (1 Thessalonians 2:2) [11, 51, 76, 91, 145, 163, 209, 526, 657, 1031, 1033, 1081, 1398, 1406, 1431, 1448, 1461, 1503, 1670, Conversation History]. You must “discipline your body and bring it into subjection,” for “your life is not your own” and you must “stand fast in the faith, be brave, be strong” (1 Corinthians 6:19; 9:27; 16:13) [11, 12, 13, 20, 79, 101, 116, 169, 175, 271, 280, 771, 1056, 1138, 1262, 1406, 1502, 1503, 1515, 1670, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Civil Authority vs. Sanctuary**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “cities of refuge” protected the slayer from “private justice,” showing that God cares for the “just administration” of civil law (Numbers 35:11–12) [361, 466, 1036, 1048, 1052, 1076, 1257, 1274, 1313, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** the concept of desolation, revealing that while the church is “subject to the governing authorities” as “God’s minister to you for good,” the magistrate has no jurisdiction over the “spirit of truth” or the “worship and governance” of the assembly of the citizens of heaven (Romans 13:4; 1 Timothy 3:15) [15, 19, 75, 198, 843, 878, 1049, 1143, 1184, 1246, 1284, 1316, 1342, 1422, 1473, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: Rendering and the Exclusive Headship of Christ**

**Verse**
“And He said to them, ‘Render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s’ ” (Matthew 22:21). [705, 842, 903, 996, Conversation History]. “And He is the head of the body, the church... that in all things He may have the preeminence” (Colossians 1:18). [255, 289, 293, 414, 418, 617, 658, 659, 660, 855, 856, 1199, 1315, 1322, 1429, 1528, 1627, 1636, 1720, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **John MacArthur**—asserts that while the state is ordained to “retard the corruption” of society and “punish evildoers,” its authority is limited to the “secular arm” [15, 18, 20, 29, 75, 76, 78, 892, 1017, 1143, 1184, 1284, 1336, 1422, 1473, 1532, 1720, Conversation History]. Christ’s instruction on taxes acknowledges Caesar’s “administrative authority,” but His position as “Head of the church” is inseparable from His “preeminence” in “all things” [255, 258, 289, 293, 412, 414, 415, 418, 617, 658, 659, 660, 784, 855, 856, 889, 906, 1101, 1199, 1315, 1322, 1357, 1418, 1426, 1429, 1528, 1627, 1636, 1720, Conversation History]. To give the state jurisdiction over “worship, teaching, and mercy” is to give to Caesar what belongs solely to God, for the Father “put all things under His feet, and gave Him to be head over all things to the church” (Ephesians 1:22) [178, 179, 239, 255, 942, 1099, 1101, 1357, 1426, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by “worldly philosophy” that suggests any earthly ruler can claim Christ’s title or govern His house, for “no slave can serve two masters” (Matthew 6:24) [170, 327, 1406, 1502, 1670, Conversation History]. “Wait for His Son from heaven,” knowing that “He who has begun a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ” (Philippians 1:6; 1 Thessalonians 1:10) [5, 13, 14, 21, 24, 83, 94, 102, 109, 113, 116, 152, 192, 201, 304, 313, 315, 332, 352, 442, 470, 614, 630, 719, 745, 816, 822, 829, 830, 852, 869, 901, 920, 940, 948, 1009, 1012, 1016, 1020, 1033, 1035, 1072, 1101, 1104, 1113, 1132, 1143, 1203, 1313, 1315, 1408, 1420, 1426, 1450, 1515, 1572, 1720, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Ecclesiastical Usurpation**
In the ancient **context**, the religious leaders were exposed as “usurpers” who “neglected the weightier matters” to protect their “political status” and “ influence over the common people” (Matthew 23:23; John 11:48) [8, 14, 87, 130, 174, 176, 180, 197, 198, 204, 248, 1053, 1091, 1316, 1352, 1365, 1422, 1720, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** the structure of the household of faith, revealing that “Jesus Christ alone is the head of the church,” and for a state to offer “protection and registration” in exchange for jurisdiction is a “spirit of fraud” that “undermines the authority of Scripture” [11, 95, 122, 186, 239, 279, 284, 285, 286, 289, 293, 317, 343, 345, 348, 359, 361, 402, 403, 412, 415, 558, 598, 1233, 1314, 1411, 1418, 1503, 1528, 1627, 1636, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 4: The Peril of State-Controlled Mercy and Teaching**

**Verse**
“ ‘No one can serve two masters; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or else he will be loyal to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon’ ” (Matthew 6:24). [170, 327, 1406, 1502, 1670, Conversation History]. “For do I now persuade men, or God? Or do I seek to please men? For if I still pleased men, I would not be a bondservant of Christ” (Galatians 1:10). [169, 1335, 1340, 1406, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Scripture handles the “noise and tumult” of state overreach by reminding us that the church’s “sole objective” is to “adorn the doctrine of God” and follow the “binding and authoritative mandate” of the Word, not the “administrative orders” of monarchs [11, 12, 15, 19, 68, 101, 125, 241, 260, 284, 332, 361, 384, 530, 785, 912, 1130, 1131, 1138, 1250, 1262, 1316, 1406, 1432, 1450, 1503, 1528, 1670, 1720, Conversation History]. The church is “never entitled to employ force” or to be “subjugated” to a state that treats “suffering” as an “administrative anomaly” to be eliminated rather than a “platform where divine power is perfected in weakness” [1, 11, 13, 15, 20, 28, 101, 483, 544, 597, 599, 626, 725, 748, 869, 959, 961, 1336, 1503, 1515, Conversation History]. When a state claims authority over life and death—as in the “worst atrocity ever carried out” at the cross—it attempts to “write themselves into God’s office,” yet “God remains sovereign in the outworking of salvation” [5, 11, 15, 30, 37, 110, 324, 412, 1061, 1132, 1143, 1315, 1402, 1431, 1450, 1502, 1503, 1567, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Wait for His Son from heaven,” for though “the kings of the earth set themselves... against the LORD,” He who “sits in the heavens shall laugh” and His “everlasting dominion” is “secure” (Psalm 2:2–4; Daniel 7:14; 1 Thessalonians 1:10) [11, 14, 24, 32, 35, 37, 43, 47, 63, 92, 94, 109, 121, 147, 176, 179, 201, 210, 266, 278, 313, 352, 386, 412, 452, 455, 470, 587, 588, 602, 614, 630, 717, 788, 789, 803, 804, 815, 816, 825, 827, 852, 869, 903, 912, 917, 921, 940, 947, 948, 958, 976, 1004, 1035, 1113, 1132, 1143, 1183, 1233, 1259, 1260, 1266, 1268, 1288, 1290, 1300, 1301, 1306, 1311, 1312, 1315, 1402, 1408, 1420, 1450, 1460, 1473, 1503, 1515, 1519, 1532, 1572, 1636, 1684, 1720, Conversation History]. You can find “tranquility of soul” by “resting upon the surest foundation,” for if God has “magnified Your word above all Your name,” His “unsearchable wisdom” will preserve the church militant (Psalm 138:2; Ephesians 3:10) [11, 24, 47, 92, 121, 147, 176, 201, 239, 280, 352, 412, 602, 630, 937, 957, 1132, 1138, 1143, 1306, 1408, 1420, 1450, 1515, 1572, 1720, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 87, 147, 176, 182, 211, 222, 285, 291, 300, 314, 324, 329, 332, 361, 405, 413, 414, 444, 449, 591, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].
